subject: biology

moments.title: Lindeman's trophic dynamics
moments.body: Lindeman, 26, publishes 'The Trophic-Dynamic Aspect of Ecology' just months before dying of liver disease. He shows energy flows through ecosystems in discrete trophic levels, with ~10% efficiency at each step.
moments.takeaway: Ecology becomes quantitative. The author dies before its impact is recognised.

moments.title: Odum's ecosystem ecology
moments.body: The Odum brothers develop ecosystem-level energy budgets. Their textbook 'Fundamentals of Ecology' (1953) defines the field for a generation.
moments.takeaway: Ecology becomes a discipline with textbooks and methods.

moments.title: Silent Spring
moments.body: Carson's book exposes DDT's effects on bird populations. Bald eagles and peregrine falcons nearly extinct in the US recover after DDT is banned in 1972. The book launches the modern environmental movement.
moments.takeaway: Pesticides bioaccumulate up food chains, with catastrophic effects.

moments.title: Trophic downgrading
moments.body: Modern ecology studies how loss of apex predators cascades down food webs (wolves in Yellowstone, sharks in oceans). Trophic cascades are central to conservation.
moments.takeaway: Lindeman's framework now guides global conservation.

now.title: Where we are today
now.body: DNA metabarcoding lets ecologists identify entire food webs from environmental DNA. Camera traps and acoustic monitoring extend ecological observation. Earth-system models incorporate biosphere-atmosphere coupling.
now.open_questions: Can rewilding restore ecosystem function in human-dominated landscapes?

reflection: Lindeman died at 27 with one paper. It still defines ecology. Can one paper change a field?
